en.title: HBO's 'Lanterns' Dives Deep Into the Human Heart of Superheroism
en.summary: HBO's new DC series 'Lanterns' is here, attempting to ground cosmic powers in relatable human struggles. With a star-studded cast and a narrative that hops through time, it aims to redefine superhero storytelling for a modern audience.
en.body:
The highly anticipated **Lanterns** has finally landed on HBO, and it arrives at a pivotal moment for the DC Universe. Following the highs of **Superman** and the lows of **Supergirl**, the franchise’s future feels as uncertain as a newly formed nebula. Yet, amidst the shifting cinematic landscape, **HBO** has carved out a distinct niche for superhero storytelling on the small screen, with **Peacemaker** and **The Penguin** setting a high bar. Now, **Lanterns**, co-created by **Damon Lindelof**, **Chris Mundy**, and comic writer **Tom King**, steps into the spotlight, promising a journey that’s as unpredictable as the powers of its titular heroes.

Inspired by the gritty realism of **True Detective** and the sleek espionage of **Slow Horses**, **Lanterns** eschews a straightforward narrative for a time-jumping mystery that spans from 1996 to 2026. The core of the first season unfolds in the intervening years, introducing us to **Hal Jordan** (played with weary gravitas by **Kyle Chandler**) and **John Stewart** (brought to life by the magnetic **Aaron Pierre**). Jordan, the seasoned Green Lantern, and Stewart, a promising candidate for the mantle, are the anchors of this story. Chandler, channeling the spirit of **Sam Shepard** in **The Right Stuff**, portrays Jordan not as an invincible icon, but as a man grappling with the weight of his interstellar responsibilities, offering a deeply human perspective on what it means to be a protector.

## A Cosmic Mystery with Earthly Stakes

The series masterfully weaves a complex tapestry of events across different timelines, forcing Jordan and Stewart to confront not only external threats but also their own evolving relationship and personal demons. The critical reception has been varied, with some praising its ambitious narrative structure and character depth, while others find its tonal shifts jarring. One reviewer noted, "If **Lanterns** provided a steady surrounding frame for these two superhero figures, the tension between Jordan and Stewart would feel the way it’s probably intended to feel: like a buddy-cop dynamic, with two strong personalities struggling to find the middle ground between them." However, the show often feels "unmoored, with one foot in the comic-book superhero world and another in the world of grim prestige drama," suggesting a deliberate, albeit sometimes uneven, attempt to bridge these disparate elements.

## The Lanterns Legacy and Fan Anticipation

For fans of the Green Lantern mythos, **Lanterns** represents a significant moment. The characters of Hal Jordan and John Stewart are cornerstones of DC Comics, and their portrayal here, particularly the dynamic between the veteran and the newcomer, is a major point of discussion. The series’ commitment to exploring the human condition through the lens of these cosmic beings has resonated with a segment of the audience, even as others express skepticism. The initial buzz surrounding the show, amplified by social media chatter and early reviews, highlights the community's eagerness for a mature, character-focused superhero narrative that respects its source material while forging its own path. The mixed reviews suggest that while the show may not be universally beloved, its ambition and unique approach have certainly sparked conversation.

## What's Next

**Lanterns** premiered on **HBO** on August 16, 2026. Viewers can expect to see the unfolding mystery across its first season, with the promise of further exploration into the complex lives of Hal Jordan and John Stewart in potential future installments.

content_raw: The highly anticipated “Lanterns” drops on HBO at an interesting time for the DC Universe. 2025’s “ Superman ” was a critical and commercial smash, a sign that maybe new head James Gunn was steering this ship in the right direction, but 2026’s “ Supergirl ” was a disaster, and audiences seem a bit skeptical that “Clayface” is what the franchise needs right now. Gunn is hard at work on 2027’s “Man of Tomorrow,” but the future of these films still feels a bit uncertain. However, superhero fiction has taken a different shape on HBO with the well-liked “ Peacemaker ,” critical darling “ The Penguin ” (not technically part of Gunn’s purview, but associated in people’s minds), and now this weekend’s “Lanterns,” a project co-created by Damon Lindelof, who has proven he can shape this kind of material in a special way with the incredible “ Watchmen .” The “Lost” and “The Leftovers” co-creator collaborates here with Chris Mundy and comic book writer Tom King to deliver the confident, engaging “Lanterns,” a show that, befitting its characters who can create something out of thin air, is never quite what you think it’s going to be. Reportedly inspired by “ True Detective ” and “ Slow Horses ,” HBO’s “Lanterns” is a time-jumping mystery, a show that moves from 1996 to 2016 to 2026. The bulk of the first season takes place in that middle period, where we meet Hal Jordan ( Kyle Chandler ) and John Stewart ( Aaron Pierre ), the nation’s Green Lantern and possibly the next to hold that title, respectively. A former test pilot, Jordan was chosen by the Green Lantern Corps to be the interstellar peacekeeper that the Earth needs, but this vision of Hal isn’t your typical hero. Reportedly inspired by Sam Shepard’s work in “ The Right Stuff ,” Chandler gives Jordan the kind of deep cynicism that comes from being an underappreciated savior of the universe. We’ve seen this kind of character a lot recently as the cost of heroism has been refracted through shows like “Watchmen” and “The Boys,” but Chandler leans into his grounded screen presence well. Strangely enough, there are echoes of Eric Taylor from “Friday Night Lights” in this performance, as if Coach suddenly had to go from training young men to saving their lives: A blend of pride and exhaustion. Lanterns (HBO Max) That pride is challenged by the very existence of a Green Lantern recruit by his side. In the premiere, Jordan puts Stewart through the motions, sending his car off the cliff so John will use the ring to save himself at the last second. He’s essentially hazing Stewart, but what becomes one of the most interesting throughlines of season one is what’s underneath that behavior: A concern that Stewart isn’t an alternate; he’s a replacement. This creates a rivalry between these two very different performers that gives “Lanterns” most of its juice through their arcs toward the title Green Lantern.
